mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tiny home on wheels and a tiny home with a foundation for rental purposes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference for rental purposes lies in their legal classification and permanence. A tiny home on wheels (THOW) is often considered an RV or recreational vehicle, potentially limiting its use as a permanent rental unit in some jurisdictions. It offers mobility but may face restrictions on long-term occupancy or placement. A tiny home on a foundation is typically classified as a permanent structure, like an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU), making it generally easier to permit and use for long-term residential rental income, subject to local zoning laws.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tiny homes on wheels are often classified as RVs, potentially limiting long-term rental use, while foundation-based tiny homes are permanent structures, generally easier to permit for residential rentals.
